why: Both moved the same two client constructions with the same reversibility, but B's judgment reaches the bar the task sets: it caught a real user-facing break (the translated stream's leading content "" chunk making OpenAIAgentWorker latch is_function=False, so every chat turn returned empty and skipped its tools), reproduced it with no Router involved, and then asked the questions a CTO asks — split the retrieval model from the chat model on a measured 12:3 request ratio, delete the quantitative agent's round trip to a tool that takes no arguments, and fix an embedding model the app never actually selected (model_type= swallowed, so every vector is ada-002 at 5x the price of the 3-small it imports). A is the more rigorous engineer — more measured on the real Router, more shipped and validated, honest that the -60% model saving costs 18 user-visible seconds — but its improvement set is a migration tune-up: labels, timeout, tier pin, one fallback, and no item that questions whether a call should exist or reaches rework scale.
A_best: Measurement discipline that changed conclusions rather than decorating them: real usage.cost and full-RAG-turn latency for four candidate models, the discovery that llama-index 0.4.7 raises ValueError on Router catalog ids (so model choice must go through policy model_map, not an env var), and the capability guard silently dropping claude-haiku-5-5 because the chat client sends temperature=0 — which is why its fallback candidate is deepseek-v4-flash and is verified falling through three ways.
B_best: Finding and proving the streaming regression that no test could catch, and then the two non-obvious system findings: the per-document quantitative agent burning an LLM round trip to produce arguments for a (*args, **kwargs) tool that always fetches the same polygon.io data, and the silently unselected embedding model that degrades every downstream answer — each with the honest cost (frontend event changes, a vector backfill with no crash to warn you).
A_worst: It never questions the application's shape: no item proposes removing an LLM call, no rework-level item exists, the one model decision is deferred to a shadow run, and it misses both the embedding misconfiguration and the argument-free tool loop — so the deliverable is a well-instrumented version of the same system rather than a better one.
B_worst: Two of its proposals are mechanically wrong in ways A measured: i1 says the model split is 'a second setting plus a second model name', but llama-index rejects gpt-5-nano before any request is made, and i3's claude-haiku-5-5 retrieval fallback is the exact candidate the capability guard drops as a silent no-op; it also hand-edits the vendored runtime (flagged twice by the outside check) and leaves tools.py:152 unverified by that check.
